newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TAYLOR'S MAIDEN CENTURY REVIVES AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR'S MAIDEN CENTURY REVIVES AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Captain Mark Taylor scored his maiden international one-day century to carry Australia to 215 for seven against India in their Titan Cup triangular series match on Monday.

Opting to bat first in the 50-over match, Australia made an inauspicious start slipping to 23 for two before Taylor combined with Steve Waugh in a 92-run stand to revive their hopes of setting a decent target.
Taylor, who survived a chance when he was 53, hammered 105 off 144 balls, including nine boundaries.
Taylor's previous best in a one-day international was 97 against New Zealand in Auckland last year.
The Australian captain had a stroke of luck midway through his innings, Rahul Dravid failing to hold on to a catch at deep square-leg off the bowling of Sachin Tendulkar.
Australia lost opener Mark Waugh for four and Michael Slater for three, both to paceman Venkatesh Prasad.
Steve Waugh hit two boundaries in his 41 off 61 balls before holing out to Saurav Ganguly at long-off.

Michael Bevan, who scored 36 off 49 deliveries, shared a 66-run stand with Taylor for the fourth wicket before Taylor mistimed an intended pull against Tendulkar and was caught by Mohammad Azharuddin at mid-wicket.
Prasad was the pick of India's bowlers finishing with three for 37 from his 10 overs.
